questions.title: Ticket Buying Simulation
questions.content:
There are n people standing in a queue where the ith person wants to buy tickets[i] tickets.

Each person can buy only one ticket at a time. After buying a ticket, they move to the end of the queue if they still need more tickets.

Return the time taken for the person at index k to finish buying tickets.
questions.outputFormat: Return total time for person k to finish buying tickets.

solutions.title: Queue implementation - Python
solutions.code:
import sys,re
nums=list(map(int,re.findall(r'-?\d+',sys.stdin.read())))
k=nums[-1]
tickets=nums[:-1]
time=0
for i in range(len(tickets)):
 if i<=k:
  time+=min(tickets[i],tickets[k])
 else:
  time+=min(tickets[i],tickets[k]-1)
print(time)

questions.title: First Unique Number in Stream
questions.content:
Design a data structure that supports:
- Show the first unique number in a queue.
- Add numbers to the queue.

Implement the FirstUnique class:
- FirstUnique(nums)
- showFirstUnique()
- add(value)
questions.inputFormat: Initialize with nums, then operations add() and showFirstUnique().

solutions.title: Queue implementation - Python
solutions.code:
import sys
from collections import deque, Counter
import re

class FirstUnique:

    def __init__(self, nums):
        self.q = deque(nums)
        self.count = Counter(nums)

    def showFirstUnique(self):
        while self.q and self.count[self.q[0]] > 1:
            self.q.popleft()
        return self.q[0] if self.q else -1

    def add(self, value):
        self.count[value] += 1
        self.q.append(value)


line = sys.stdin.read().strip()

# extract nums
nums_match = re.search(r"nums=\[(.*?)\]", line)
nums = []
if nums_match:
    nums = list(map(int, nums_match.group(1).split(","))) if nums_match.group(1) else []

q = FirstUnique(nums)

# remove nums part
ops_part = re.sub(r"nums=\[.*?\],?\s*", "", line)

ops = [x.strip() for x in ops_part.split(",") if x.strip()]
res = []

for op in ops:

    if op.startswith("add"):
        val = int(op[4:-1])
        q.add(val)

    elif op.startswith("showFirstUnique"):
        res.append(str(q.showFirstUnique()))

print(",".join(res))

questions.title: Maximum Robots Within Budget
questions.content:
You are given arrays chargeTimes and runningCosts and an integer budget.

The cost of running k robots is:
max(chargeTimes) + k * sum(runningCosts)

Find the maximum number of robots that can run simultaneously without exceeding the budget.
questions.inputFormat: Arrays chargeTimes, runningCosts, and integer budget.

solutions.title: Queue implementation - Python
solutions.code:
import sys,re
from collections import deque

def maximumRobots(charge, run, budget):

    q=deque()
    total=0
    left=0
    ans=0

    for right in range(len(charge)):

        while q and charge[q[-1]]<=charge[right]:
            q.pop()
        q.append(right)

        total+=run[right]

        while q and charge[q[0]]+(right-left+1)*total>budget:
            if q[0]==left:
                q.popleft()
            total-=run[left]
            left+=1

        ans=max(ans,right-left+1)

    return ans


line=sys.stdin.read().strip()

charge=list(map(int,re.search(r"charge=\[(.*?)\]",line).group(1).split(",")))
run=list(map(int,re.search(r"run=\[(.*?)\]",line).group(1).split(",")))
budget=int(re.search(r"budget=(\d+)",line).group(1))

print(maximumRobots(charge,run,budget))

Given a circular integer array nums, return the maximum possible sum of a non-empty subarray.

A circular array means the end connects to the beginning.

solutions.title: Queue implementation - Python

import sys, re

def maxSubarraySumCircular(nums):
    total = sum(nums)
    curMax = curMin = 0
    maxSum = minSum = nums[0]

    for n in nums:
        curMax = max(curMax + n, n)
        maxSum = max(maxSum, curMax)

        curMin = min(curMin + n, n)
        minSum = min(minSum, curMin)

    return maxSum if maxSum < 0 else max(maxSum, total - minSum)

questions.title: K Empty Slots Problem
questions.content:
You are given an array bulbs where bulbs[i] is the position of the bulb turned on at day i+1.

Return the earliest day when there exist two turned-on bulbs with exactly k bulbs between them that are off.

solutions.title: Queue implementation - Python
solutions.code:
import sys,re

def kEmptySlots(bulbs,k):
    n=len(bulbs)
    days=[0]*n

    for day,pos in enumerate(bulbs,1):
        days[pos-1]=day

    res=float('inf')
    left,right=0,k+1

    while right<n:
        valid=True

        for i in range(left+1,right):
            if days[i] < max(days[left],days[right]):
                left=i
                right=i+k+1
                valid=False
                break

        if valid:
            res=min(res,max(days[left],days[right]))
            left=right
            right=left+k+1

    return -1 if res==float('inf') else res


line=sys.stdin.read().strip()

nums=list(map(int,re.findall(r'\d+',line)))

k=nums[-1]
bulbs=nums[:-1]

print(kEmptySlots(bulbs,k))

questions.title: Rotting Oranges Simulation
questions.content:
You are given a grid where:
- 0 represents an empty cell
- 1 represents a fresh orange
- 2 represents a rotten orange

Every minute, any fresh orange adjacent (up, down, left, right) to a rotten orange becomes rotten.

Return the minimum number of minutes required so that no fresh orange remains. If this is impossible, return -1.
questions.outputFormat: Return minimum minutes until all oranges rot.

solutions.title: Queue implementation - Python
solutions.code:
import sys
import re
from collections import deque

def orangesRotting(grid):
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    q = deque()
    fresh = 0

    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            if grid[r][c] == 2:
                q.append((r, c, 0))
            elif grid[r][c] == 1:
                fresh += 1

    dirs = [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)]
    time = 0

    while q:
        r, c, t = q.popleft()
        time = max(time, t)

        for dr, dc in dirs:
            nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols and grid[nr][nc] == 1:
                grid[nr][nc] = 2
                fresh -= 1
                q.append((nr, nc, t + 1))

    return time if fresh == 0 else -1


line = sys.stdin.read().strip()

# extract rows
rows = re.findall(r'\[([0-9,]+)\]', line)

grid = [list(map(int, r.split(','))) for r in rows]

print(orangesRotting(grid))

Initially, add all rotten oranges coordinates to a queue. For each minute, process all oranges currently in the queue.
Count the total number of fresh oranges and decrement it as they rot; if it reaches 0, you've found the time.

import sys
import ast
from collections import deque

line=sys.stdin.read().strip()
board_str=line.split("=",1)[1]
board=ast.literal_eval(board_str)

n=len(board)

def id2pos(s):
    r=(s-1)//n
    c=(s-1)%n
    if r%2==1:
        c=n-1-c
    return n-1-r,c

q=deque([(1,0)])
visited=set([1])

while q:
    s,steps=q.popleft()

    if s==n*n:
        print(steps)
        sys.exit()

    for i in range(1,7):
        ns=s+i
        if ns>n*n:
            break

        r,c=id2pos(ns)

        if board[r][c]!=-1:
            ns=board[r][c]

        if ns not in visited:
            visited.add(ns)
            q.append((ns,steps+1))

print(-1)

questions.title: Longest Continuous Subarray Within Limit
questions.content:
Given an integer array nums and an integer limit, return the length of the longest continuous subarray such that the absolute difference between the maximum and minimum elements is less than or equal to limit.

Use an efficient approach to maintain the max and min values in the sliding window.
questions.outputFormat: Return the length of the longest valid subarray.

solutions.title: Queue implementation - Python
solutions.code:
import sys
from collections import deque

line = sys.stdin.read().strip()

nums_part = line[line.index('[')+1:line.index(']')]
nums = list(map(int, nums_part.split(',')))

limit = int(line.split("limit=")[1])

def longestSubarray(nums, limit):
    maxd = deque()
    mind = deque()
    left = 0
    res = 0

    for right, val in enumerate(nums):
        while maxd and val > maxd[-1]:
            maxd.pop()
        while mind and val < mind[-1]:
            mind.pop()

        maxd.append(val)
        mind.append(val)

        while maxd[0] - mind[0] > limit:
            if nums[left] == maxd[0]:
                maxd.popleft()
            if nums[left] == mind[0]:
                mind.popleft()
            left += 1

        res = max(res, right - left + 1)

    return res

print(longestSubarray(nums, limit))

questions.title: Sliding Window Maximum
questions.content:
Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return an array containing the maximum value in each sliding window of size k.

Use an efficient deque-based approach with O(n) complexity.

solutions.title: Queue implementation - Python
solutions.code:
import sys
from collections import deque

line = sys.stdin.read().strip()

nums_part = line[line.index('[')+1:line.index(']')]
nums = list(map(int, nums_part.split(',')))

k = int(line.split("k=")[1])

def maxSlidingWindow(nums, k):
    dq = deque()
    res = []

    for i, n in enumerate(nums):

        while dq and nums[dq[-1]] <= n:
            dq.pop()

        dq.append(i)

        if dq[0] == i - k:
            dq.popleft()

        if i >= k - 1:
            res.append(nums[dq[0]])

    return res

ans = maxSlidingWindow(nums, k)
print("[" + ",".join(map(str, ans)) + "]")

questions.title: Minimum K Consecutive Bit Flips
questions.content:
You are given a binary array nums and an integer k. In one operation, you can flip a subarray of length k (change 0 to 1 and 1 to 0).

Return the minimum number of flips required so that there are no 0s in the array. If it is impossible, return -1.
questions.inputFormat: Binary array nums and integer k.

solutions.title: Queue implementation - Python
solutions.code:
import sys
from collections import deque

line = sys.stdin.read().strip()

nums_part = line[line.index('[')+1:line.index(']')]
nums = list(map(int, nums_part.split(',')))

k = int(line.split("k=")[1])

def minKBitFlips(nums, k):
    dq = deque()
    flips = 0
    n = len(nums)

    for i in range(n):

        if dq and dq[0] == i:
            dq.popleft()

        if (nums[i] + len(dq)) % 2 == 0:

            if i + k > n:
                return -1

            flips += 1
            dq.append(i + k)

    return flips

print(minKBitFlips(nums, k))

questions.title: Shortest Subarray With Sum At Least K
questions.content:
Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the length of the shortest non-empty subarray with sum at least k.

If no such subarray exists, return -1.

Efficient solutions use prefix sums and a monotonic deque.
questions.outputFormat: Return length of shortest valid subarray.

solutions.title: Queue implementation - Python
solutions.code:
import sys
from collections import deque

line = sys.stdin.read().strip()

nums_part = line[line.index('[')+1:line.index(']')]
nums = list(map(int, nums_part.split(',')))

k = int(line.split("k=")[1])

def shortestSubarray(nums, k):
    n = len(nums)

    prefix = [0]*(n+1)
    for i in range(n):
        prefix[i+1] = prefix[i] + nums[i]

    dq = deque()
    res = n+1

    for i in range(n+1):

        while dq and prefix[i] - prefix[dq[0]] >= k:
            res = min(res, i - dq.popleft())

        while dq and prefix[i] <= prefix[dq[-1]]:
            dq.pop()

        dq.append(i)

    return res if res <= n else -1


print(shortestSubarray(nums, k))
